newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended lower on Thursday before the release of June consumer price data, tracking other continental markets lower as a new bout of EMU's doubts hit European debt.

"Tietmeyer's remarks early today awoke same doubts. The market reacted well but I still think tomorrow the focus will remain on Germany where he is expected to attend the cabinet meeting for the mini-budget," a dealer in Madrid said.
Earlier, Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said that in convergence toward Europe's single currency not only the three percent deficit criteria must be taken into account.
Other factors, such as debt, should also be monitored.
On Friday, Tietmeyer and Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing are expected to attend a cabinet meeting in Bonn.
The domestic focus will be on June's CPI, which analysts expect at 1.5/1.6 percent year on year after 1.5 percent in May.
"At least this is what the market is discounting. I do not think a value like that would be able to move prices," a dealer said.
He added that Friday the market would likely continue today's consolidation in a possible trading range between support at 116.90 and resistance at 117.70.
